conclusion: CPCB's October-2025 assessment classifies the Arkavathi (Hesaraghatta reservoir to downstream Kanakapura) as Priority I - its worst band - with BOD up to 72 mg/L, up from Priority III in 2018. The polluted reach grew from 66 km to 104 km over the same period, extending upstream into Bengaluru's urban core.
growthNote: Almost all of the 2025 growth is upstream: the new length sits in Bengaluru North and Yelahanka, with Bangalore-South roughly doubling. The central (Ramanagara, Magadi) and southern (Kanakapura) reaches were already mapped as polluted in 2020.
priorityNote: Priority is CPCB's BOD-based class (V in 2011, III in 2018). On the same 2022-23 data the boards diverge: CPCB reads Priority I, but KSPCB's own lab analysis (in the Feb-2026 NMCG report) reads Priority IV. The June-2025 NMCG report still listed III, predating the October reclassification. Lengths shown are Paani Earth's mapping (CPCB did not specify a length).
mprOverview: Tracked under NGT order OA 673/2018 through monthly NMCG progress reports (2020-2026), which itemise the two stretch ULBs - Ramanagara and Kanakapura - and the V-Valley catchment as the upstream source.
reportingCaveat: Figures here are what the official documents (NMCG MPRs, District Environment Plans) report. Where something shows as nil, not submitted, or unmentioned, it means it is not recorded in those documents - it may still be present or happening on the ground, or held in non-public records.
levelCoverage: Sewage and solid waste are reported at ULB (town) level - yearly for Ramanagara and Kanakapura, a single DEP snapshot for Magadi, Harohalli and Bidadi. Hazardous and biomedical waste are reported at district level (Bengaluru Urban, Ramanagara); industrial effluent at the V-Valley catchment. No Gram-Panchayat-level data appears in the reports we have reviewed, and rural taluk areas outside the towns are not separately reported.
bodCaveat: CPCB priority is based on BOD alone, from grab samples. BOD is a concentration: a high value can mean more organic pollution OR less dilution in low-flow months, or both - so it needs flow context. It also misses heavy metals, which independent studies have repeatedly documented along this river.

evidence.headline: Pollution here is documented consistently over years - and well beyond the single BOD number.
points: CPCB Oct-2025 monitoring: max BOD 72 mg/L at Hesaraghatta, 46 d/s Kanakapura, 21 Tippagondanahalli, 11 Manchanabale.
NWMP monitoring (Mar 2024-May 2025): BOD up to 30 mg/L at Thippagondanahalli and 52 mg/L d/s Kanakapura; dissolved oxygen frequently below 4 mg/L.
ATREE: heavy metals found in milk, fodder and vegetables in villages along the Vrishabhavathi.
Arkavathi Horata Samithi and Paani Earth: RTI-sourced lab analyses.

tabs.intro: Government reports state that no industrial effluent reaches the river. Below is what each public record reports.
tabs.summaryLine: Reports claim 100% treatment; no CETP reported; industries 144 to 191

categories.label: Discharges
categories.body: Government reports claim 100% treatment and zero discharge to the river. The F-register records ~5.65 MLD of industrial effluent from 562 units (2021); BBMP's Vrishabhavathi valley alone reports 25.34 MLD of trade effluent (DEP 2022).
points: V-Valley catchment (drains to the Arkavathi): ~4.7 MLD trade effluent, reported essentially unchanged across the NMCG MPRs 2020-2025.
Industries in the V-Valley catchment grew 144 (2020) -> 181 (2022) -> 191 (2025); 14 units connected to a common ETP, unchanged 2022-2025 (NMCG MPRs).
Ramanagara DEP (2021): effluent "fully recycled, zero discharge"; 581 industries "meeting standards".
CAG (2017): 38 of 66 sampled KIADB areas had no CETP; ~2,571 ML/yr discharged untreated.
The DEP self-report and the CAG audit report different findings.

categories.label: Industrial areas
categories.body: Common effluent treatment plant (CETP) coverage of the industrial areas along the stretch:
points: No CETP reported in Ramanagara district (DEP 2021).
Harohalli KIADB (1st-4th phases): nearest common ETP >20 km (Neer Vazhvu estimate).
Across the basin ~26 of 56 industrial areas have no CETP within ~5 km (8 of 18 KIADB).

categories.label: Contaminated clusters
categories.body: Officially recognised pollution hotspots along the stretch:
points: Peenya (Vrishabhavathi valley): CPCB Critically Polluted Area, CEPI 78.12; NGT OA 1038/2018.
Mavallipura dumpsite (Yelahanka): manganese in groundwater - Bengaluru Urban's recorded contaminated site.
Hazardous waste: no TSDF or SLF reported in Bengaluru Urban; 1,718 HW-generating industries (DEP 2022).

industries.note: The stretch drains Bengaluru's south and west industrial belt - the Bidadi, Harohalli and KIADB clusters. Which units discharge into it directly versus through the secondary and tertiary drain network is not yet traced (see gaps below). Open the Pressures floor to see industrial areas and their CETP coverage.
